Now the sun was sinking into the Pacific, the last tamal sat wrapped in its husk, and a customer was holding out a bill for it. Consuelo took the tamal from the steamer, looked down the promenade at the boy hurrying toward them, and set it in Tomoe's hands instead. 'Check,' Maya said, though no board lay between us,
only the boarding-house kettle and two cracked cups.
All week the club had whispered of my blunder,
the queen I'd left hanging like wash in the Haifa wind,
and Maya, smug as a bishop, had told it best.
So I, Dvora, came down to the kitchen armed with silence,

But she poured the tea, and slid the sugar toward me,

to a man who never let her forget it.

two old rivals, the game between us set down.

It recounts a family dispute over land and ends with the sons agreeing to sell it.
It presents a belief shared by the narrator and a family, then shows an outsider overturning it.
It contrasts two cities' craft traditions before describing the narrator's departure.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자와 가족은 과수원이 버려졌다고 믿으며, 아들들은 땅을 팔자고 말한다. 외부인인 구매자가 쓰러진 나무를 만져 보고 20년 동안 건조 중이라고 밝히자 화자는 비로소 나무의 간격과 벗긴 껍질을 새롭게 본다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 구매 목록이 없고, B는 땅을 파는 결말이 없으며, D는 두 도시의 전통을 비교하지 않는다.

seed.conflict: while deciding whether a rule still applies
seed.topicSeed: a mountain bus stop in Dakar; an author and her translator while deciding whether a rule still applies

g.passage: Dakar was still asleep when the author Nneka and her translator, Babatunde, sat down at the bus stop on the hill road, where an old rule was painted on a board: Wait for the third bus; the first two belong to the goats. Nneka laughed and stood when the first bus came. Babatunde did not. 'In the story my village tells,' he said, 'a herder painted that rule after his goats were nearly crushed on this bend. The goats are gone, but he did not make the rule for goats alone.' Nneka sat back down, uncertain. The first bus passed, then the second, both crowded and swaying dangerously around the curve. When the third arrived, nearly empty, she climbed aboard, opened her notebook, and asked Babatunde how the herder's words should sound in her book.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A journey is planned, a delay occurs, and the characters abandon their trip entirely.
A legend is retold in full before the narrator explains its moral to the reader.
Two characters argue about a translation until one of them quits the project.
A rule is mocked, its origin is explained, and events lead a character to reconsider it.
g.explanation: Nneka는 처음에 표지판의 규칙을 비웃고 첫 버스에 오르려 한다. Babatunde가 규칙이 생긴 마을 이야기를 들려준 뒤, 앞의 두 버스가 위험하게 흔들리며 지나가는 사건이 이어지고 Nneka는 규칙을 다시 생각해 자기 책에 담으려 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 여행을 포기하지 않고, B는 전설을 전부 다시 들려주거나 화자가 교훈을 설명하지 않으며, C는 번역을 둘러싼 다툼이 없다.

seed.relationship: two neighbors with a shared wall
seed.conflict: while pretending to enjoy a gift that is wrong
seed.topicSeed: a beekeeper's yard in Jeju Island; two neighbors with a shared wall while pretending to enjoy a gift that is wrong

g.passage: Minjun found the gift on the shared wall between their yards on Jeju Island: a jar of honey, labeled in Younghee's careful hand, tied with red string. He tasted it at once and winced. It was buckwheat honey, dark and bitter, the kind his own hives produced, the kind he had complained about to her all summer. Still, when Younghee peered over the wall that evening, he smacked his lips and praised its depth. __She beamed and confessed that she had traded three of her best jars for it, certain he had been hinting all along.__ Minjun kept smiling. The next morning he left a jar of his own buckwheat honey on the wall, labeled in his clumsiest hand, and waited to see whether she would pretend too.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals Younghee misread Minjun's complaints, raising the stakes of his pretense.
It shows that Younghee knew all along that Minjun disliked buckwheat honey.
It explains why Minjun decides to stop keeping bees on Jeju Island at last.
It introduces a rivalry between the neighbors over whose honey sells best.
g.explanation: 앞에서 Minjun은 여름 내내 메밀꿀에 대해 불평했는데도 맛있는 척 칭찬한다. 밑줄 친 문장은 Younghee가 그 불평을 넌지시 원한다는 뜻으로 오해했고, 자기 좋은 꿀 세 병까지 내주었음을 드러내 그의 거짓 칭찬이 더 무거워지게 만든다. 이것이 다음 날 Minjun이 꿀을 되돌려 놓는 행동으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Younghee가 오해했다는 내용과 반대이고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

seed.topicSeed: a salt-water pool in Kingston; a stepfather and his stepdaughter about moving an elderly parent

g.passage: Ten slow laps in the salt-water pool off Kingston harbor: that was how my stepfather and I had always avoided talking. I was Janelle, nineteen, and he still called me 'the girl' to his friends, not unkindly. That morning we had to decide whether to move his mother, Kiara, out of the house in Port Royal where she had lived for sixty years and into our spare room. I expected him to insist; he was a man who liked decisions made. Instead, between laps, he floated on his back and told me how she had taught him to swim in this very pool, holding his chin above the water. __Then he asked what I thought she would want, and he waited for my answer.__ For the first time, I saw him not as my mother's husband but as a son afraid of choosing wrong.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows the stepfather testing the narrator before announcing a decision already made.
It explains why the family ultimately decides to keep Kiara in her house in Port Royal.
It marks a change in the stepfather's manner, showing he values the narrator's judgment.
It reveals the narrator's resentment at being asked to decide for the whole family.
g.explanation: 화자는 결정을 밀어붙이기 좋아하는 의붓아버지가 자기 뜻을 고집할 것이라고 예상했고, 그는 친구들에게 화자를 '그 아이'라고 부르던 사람이다. 밑줄 친 문장에서 그는 화자의 생각을 묻고 대답을 기다리며, 예상과 다른 태도로 화자의 판단을 존중한다. 이 변화가 마지막에 화자가 그를 두려워하는 아들로 보게 되는 계기가 되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이미 정한 결정이 있다는 근거가 없고, B는 최종 결정이 나오지 않으며, D는 화자의 원망이 드러나지 않는다.
